'sample_number' (declared range [0.2, 1.2]): a margin-based review set (olmoearth_review_set_from_result) ranks a band's windows by their distance from a decision threshold, and this band has none: it has no margins, no 'most ambiguous' or lowest-margin windows and no per-class review; a review set of this band needs a threshold for it (olmoearth_review_set_from_result takes 'threshold')

the results measure different properties (['sample_karst_score', 'sample_number']): a difference, ratio, average, RMSE, agreement share or any other statistic that combines the two quantities means nothing, and neither reads higher or lower than the other; only each map's own mean and the correlation are returned

no labels were given to this comparison, which takes none: nothing here says which map is right, more accurate or better, and nothing here says whether labels for these maps exist (none was looked up); the correlation says only whether the two rise and fall together

labels drawn only from the low-confidence, least certain or most ambiguous windows (or from a review set) are not a sample of the map: an error rate over them describes those windows and overstates the map's, so it is no defensible error rate for either map; each of olmoearth_plan_label_sample's designs ('confidence', 'proportional', 'random') draws from every window of the map, and its estimate needs every drawn window labelled

a correlation is one number pooled over all the compared cells and has no location: it cannot say where the maps agree or differ, that they agree or differ anywhere or nowhere, that large parts agree while the rest differs, or that one is high where the other is low; only a per-window value, which a correlation is not, can place them

r = -0.0172 over 25 cells, 95% interval -0.41 to 0.38: an interval that holds both no relation and a moderate one cannot say whether the maps co-vary, so neither 'they do not agree at all', 'independent', 'unrelated' or 'effectively zero' nor 'they agree' follows from it; more cells narrow the interval

content:
I found both 2025 runs (completed, same PA area, period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31) and ran a cross-model comparison over their shared extent (~10,091 km²). Two important caveats come out of it.

**Key finding: the two maps predict different quantities.**

| Run | Model | Band (declared range) | Result id |
|---|---|---|---|
| KarstBinary (pred `dd504793`) | fine-tuned, per-pixel regression | `sample_karst_score` [0.0, 1.0] | `419c581d` |
| KarstNumber (pred `a83ca800`) | fine-tuned, per-pixel regression | `sample_number` [0.2, 1.2] | `afb1cf68` |

Because the bands are different units, a direct "difference / agreement" between them would mix two quantities, so none is computed — only whether they rise and fall together:

- **Correlation: r = −0.0172** (25 of 36 grid cells compared; 11 dropped as no-data; 95% interval −0.41 to 0.38). That interval spans zero, so this sample **cannot say whether the maps co-vary at all** — the signal is consistent with no relationship and with a moderate one.

**Which is right?** Not answerable from this run: no ground truth was involved, and nothing here measures either map's accuracy. (Both models were fine-tuned on separate Studio label fields, but this run looked up no labels for this area.) A map-vs-map comparison tells you how they relate, never which matches the ground.

**To settle "which is right", options within this agent's capabilities:**
1. You supply reference labels at specific points → I run `olmoearth_classification_metrics` on named thresholds, giving per-class accuracy/IoU per map.
2. Name a threshold per band → I plan a label sample (`olmoearth_plan_label_sample`) and later estimate each map's error rate from your reviewer labels (`olmoearth_estimate_map_error`).

Want me to go with option 1 (tell me coordinates or points you have labels for) or plan option 2?
